andronis-boutique-vs-canaves-oia-suites.title: Andronis Boutique or Canaves Oia Suites | Suites With Keith
andronis-boutique-vs-canaves-oia-suites.description: The two hotels at the top of Keith's Santorini ranking, minutes apart in Oia. He toured both on the same trip — here's how to decide between them.
andronis-boutique-vs-canaves-oia-suites.deck: These are #01 and #02 on my Santorini ranking, minutes apart in Oia, and the comparison I’m asked to settle most on the island. I toured both on the same trip. The decision comes down to which room you’ve been picturing.
andronis-boutique-vs-canaves-oia-suites.stamp: Toured same trip · #01 and #02 on my Santorini ranking · both preferred partners

choose.h3: If you’re dreaming of the cave room
choose.lead: Authentic cave-style suites, recently renovated — marble, wooden arches, surprisingly bright interiors — with a plunge pool or jacuzzi in every single room. These are the rooms people actually picture when they book Santorini.
choose.alt: Cave-style suite terrace at Andronis Boutique, Oia

choose.h3: If you want the caldera, perfected
choose.lead: Completely renovated, and it blew me away everywhere I looked — the finishes, the water features, the landscaping. It sits higher on the Caldera than most, which buys something genuinely rare on Santorini: privacy.
choose.alt: Caldera suites at Canaves Oia Suites, Santorini

rows: Plunge pool or jacuzzi in every room, no exceptions
Private water features — but not in every category
The River Pool Suite — best suite I saw across 38 hotels
Spa devotees should look at sister property Andronis Concept
The best spa product on the Caldera, plus a large gym
Two- and three-bedroom pool villas — nearly nonexistent in Oia
andronis-boutique-vs-canaves-oia-suites.footnote: Both are preferred partners — book either through me and the rate is identical to booking direct, with the partner extras layered on. One planning note: Canaves Oia Suites is 13+; traveling with younger kids, sister property Canaves Epitome, a short walk away, has no age restrictions.

verdict.h2: If the River Pool Suite is available for your dates, stop deliberating.
paras: Canaves Oia Suites was the best hotel I saw for first-time visitors to Santorini, and I’d be hard pressed to recommend anything else first for the classic caldera-luxury experience. Complete privacy doesn’t exist anywhere on the Caldera, but Canaves does a particularly good job of engineering it — set higher than most, with coverings above every room’s outdoor space.

But Andronis Boutique’s rooms are the real thing — genuine cave architecture with a water feature in every room, at rates that usually land a few hundred a night lower. Between the top Oia properties you really can’t go wrong; this one is about the picture in your head. And if you land on Boutique, book dinner at Lycabettus the moment you confirm the room.

andronis-boutique-vs-andronis-luxury-sui.title: Andronis Boutique or Andronis Luxury Suites | Suites With Keith
andronis-boutique-vs-andronis-luxury-sui.description: Same portfolio, same cliffside, two different trips. Keith toured both Andronis flagships back to back — here's which one fits which traveler.
andronis-boutique-vs-andronis-luxury-sui.deck: Same portfolio, same Oia cliffside, two very different trips. The flagship reads refined, old-school luxury; Boutique is the authentic cave-style Santorini people fly in for. I toured both back to back — here’s how I split them.
andronis-boutique-vs-andronis-luxury-sui.stamp: #02 and #04 on my Santorini ranking · same portfolio · both toured

choose.h3: If you want Santorini to look like Santorini
choose.lead: Real cave-style rooms, recently renovated, with a plunge pool or jacuzzi in every one. It skews toward younger honeymooners, and rates tend to land below the flagship — while giving up very little.
choose.alt: Renovated cave interiors at Andronis Boutique

choose.h3: If refined and looked-after is the point
choose.lead: The flagship: elegant, more exclusive on paper, all 39 suites and villas with a water feature, and home to Lycabettus — the island’s most famous cliffside table. Also the portfolio’s best choice when mobility is a factor.
choose.alt: Cliffside pools at Andronis Luxury Suites, Oia

rows: Spacious and refined — old-school luxury more than Cycladic
Every room — plunge pool or jacuzzi
All 39 — plunge pool, jacuzzi, or full pool in the villas
40+ couples, anniversaries — returning since the honeymoon
Like most of Oia, stairs come with the territory
A few suites near check-in have only 15–20 stairs
Lycabettus — plus a MINI Cooper Cabrio with select suites
andronis-boutique-vs-andronis-luxury-sui.footnote: Whichever you book, reserve Lycabettus the same day you confirm the room — it fills faster than the hotel does. And both are preferred partners: same rate as booking direct, with the extras layered on.

verdict.h2: Boutique for the honeymoon; the flagship for the anniversary.
paras: Luxury Suites lends itself perfectly to a 50+ clientele on anniversary trips — or couples returning to Santorini for the first time since their honeymoon. It’s equally beautiful, just more old-school luxury than authentically Santorini, and that’s exactly why it works for that trip. It’s also my pick in the portfolio when mobility is a concern.
For everyone else: Boutique’s cave-style rooms are the real thing, you give up very little versus the flagship, and you usually pay less doing it.

andronis-boutique-vs-andronis-luxury-sui.subject: Andronis Boutique vs Luxury Suites Inquiry

andronis-luxury-suites-vs-canaves-ena.title: Andronis Luxury Suites or Canaves Ena | Suites With Keith
andronis-luxury-suites-vs-canaves-ena.description: The refined Andronis flagship against the freshly renovated Canaves original — #04 and #05 on Keith's Santorini ranking, and closer than the numbers suggest.
andronis-luxury-suites-vs-canaves-ena.deck: The refined flagship of one Oia dynasty against the freshly renovated original of the other — #04 and #05 on my Santorini ranking, and closer than those numbers suggest. I toured both on the same trip.
andronis-luxury-suites-vs-canaves-ena.stamp: #04 and #05 on my Santorini ranking · both toured · both preferred partners

choose.h3: If polish and ease win
choose.lead: Spacious suites with a water feature in all 39 rooms, the Mare Sanus Spa, Lycabettus at home, and the portfolio’s most manageable stairs — a few suites sit only 15–20 steps from check-in.
choose.alt: Andronis Luxury Suites on the Oia cliffside

choose.h3: If character and intimacy win
choose.lead: Eighteen suites carved from 17th-century wine caves, run by the same family since the 80s and brought fully up to date by a 2024 renovation. Higher on the Caldera — which buys real privacy — with a swim-up bar that adds rare social energy.
choose.alt: Wine-cave suites at Canaves Ena, Oia

rows: 17th-century wine caves — minimalist, renovated 2024, slightly smaller
Not every room — check your category
Adami — authentic Greek gastronomy by the main pool
The swim-up pool bar — rare on an island of couples keeping to themselves
Usually lands right where Boutique does
andronis-luxury-suites-vs-canaves-ena.footnote: Ena is framed as the accessible Canaves, but the value positioning doesn’t always show up in the rate — pricing almost always lands right where Andronis Boutique does. Judge it on the room, the privacy, the water feature, and the price for your actual dates.

verdict.h2: Flagship polish or family heritage — this one is a mood choice.
paras: If a water feature is non-negotiable, or stairs are a concern, Luxury Suites settles it — every one of its 39 rooms has a plunge pool, jacuzzi, or full pool, and it’s my pick in the portfolio when mobility is a factor.

But Ena has the most personal story on the Caldera — one family since the 80s, suites that trace to 17th-century wine caves — and the team there, especially longtime sales director Des, is a big reason I trust sending clients to the property. The intimacy is the point; just know the square footage isn’t the selling feature.

andronis-luxury-suites-vs-canaves-ena.subject: Andronis Luxury Suites vs Canaves Ena Inquiry

andronis-arcadia-vs-canaves-epitome.title: Andronis Arcadia or Canaves Epitome | Suites With Keith
andronis-arcadia-vs-canaves-epitome.description: Next-door neighbors outside Oia with the same open-Aegean sunset — one a 114-key resort with a scene, the other Keith's #01 hotel in Greece.
andronis-arcadia-vs-canaves-epitome.deck: They share a property line just outside Oia and the same golden-hour orientation — a real sunset into the open Aegean, something the Caldera hotels physically cannot offer. And they could not be aiming at more different trips. One is a true resort with a scene; the other is my favorite hotel in Greece.
andronis-arcadia-vs-canaves-epitome.stamp: Literally next door · both sunset-facing · my #01 in Greece lives here

choose.h3: If you want options and energy
choose.lead: A true resort — 114 suites and villas, every one with a private pool, including some of the island’s largest. The ARCADemy kids club gives families real infrastructure, and Pacman’s live music and Beefbar Santorini bring a scene the rest of this list doesn’t have.
choose.alt: Private pools at Andronis Arcadia, Santorini

choose.h3: If you want the private world
choose.lead: Fifty-three rooms that still feel boutique, landscaped gardens behind volcanic-rock walls, two-bedroom suites with pools and outdoor dining decks — and Omnia, the best hotel restaurant I ate at across the entire trip.
choose.alt: Gardens and pools at Canaves Epitome, near Oia

rows: Private pool in every room — some of the island’s largest
Suite pools and decks — some rooms look up into the water
A bit of a scene — two very Mykonos-esque dining options
A world away from Oia’s busy streets
The ARCADemy kids club, resort-scale grounds
No age restrictions — rare at this level of luxury
Pacman with live music, Beefbar Santorini
Omnia — worth booking even if you stay elsewhere
andronis-arcadia-vs-canaves-epitome.footnote: One practical note: Arcadia is massive and spread out — in summer heat, with no meltemi wind blowing, you’ll want a golf cart to get around. Epitome is more spread out than the Caldera hotels too, but its 53 rooms still feel boutique.

verdict.h2: Epitome — unless the scene is the point.
paras: If you’re asking me for the single best hotel I experienced across the Greek islands, it’s Canaves Epitome — perhaps one of the top three stays of my entire life. The gardens turn the common areas into a private world minutes from Oia’s crowds, the two-bedroom suites are the star, and the sunset is the best in Greece.

Arcadia is the right Santorini hotel for travelers who want activity and options rather than seclusion — and for families, the infrastructure is real; they’ll tell you the same. Great if you like a bit of a scene; not the move if you want exclusivity and quiet. Planning a wedding at either — room blocks at Arcadia, a buyout at Epitome — is exactly what I do.

andronis-arcadia-vs-canaves-epitome.subject: Andronis Arcadia vs Canaves Epitome Inquiry

canaves-oia-suites-vs-canaves-epitome.title: Canaves Oia Suites or Canaves Epitome | Suites With Keith
canaves-oia-suites-vs-canaves-epitome.description: Same family, same standard, one decision: the Caldera or the sunset. Keith's #01 in Santorini against his #01 in all of Greece.
canaves-oia-suites-vs-canaves-epitome.deck: Same family, same standard, a short walk apart — and one real decision: the Caldera or the sunset. This is #01 on my Santorini ranking against #01 on my Greece top 10, which makes it the closest call on this site.
canaves-oia-suites-vs-canaves-epitome.stamp: Sister properties · a short walk apart · my #01 twice over

choose.h3: If the postcard is non-negotiable
choose.lead: The classic caldera-luxury experience, perfected — set higher than most for privacy, completely renovated, with the best spa product on the Caldera and the single best suite I saw in Greece.
choose.alt: Caldera view from Canaves Oia Suites

choose.h3: If serenity beats the cliff
choose.lead: A short walk from Oia near Ammoudi Bay: gardens behind volcanic-rock walls, two-bedroom suites with pools and dining decks, no age restrictions, and a real sunset into the open Aegean.
choose.alt: Suite pool at Canaves Epitome

rows: On the Caldera, set higher than most
A short walk from Oia, near Ammoudi Bay
A real sunset into the open Aegean — the Caldera can’t do this
The River Pool Suite — best I saw across 38 hotels
Two-bedroom suites with pools, decks, and outdoor dining
The Caldera’s best spa, plus a large gym
Shuttle access to every Canaves property’s restaurants and spas
canaves-oia-suites-vs-canaves-epitome.footnote: Whichever you choose, book a table at Omnia — Epitome’s restaurant above Ammoudi Bay was the best hotel restaurant I ate at across the entire trip, and it’s worth the reservation even if you’re sleeping on the Caldera.

verdict.h2: First trip: the Caldera. Every trip after: Epitome.
paras: First-time visitors picturing the classic cliffside image are choosing a different experience at Epitome — and if that image is non-negotiable, book Oia Suites. It was the best hotel I saw for first-timers on the island, and I’d be hard pressed to recommend anything else first for that trip.

But the single best hotel I experienced across the Greek islands was Epitome. What the location buys you is space and serenity — a private world minutes from Oia’s crowds — plus the best sunset in Greece and dining the Caldera hotels can’t match. That’s why it holds #01 on my Greece list even ranked beside its more famous sibling.

four-seasons-napa-valley-vs-montage-heal.title: Four Seasons Napa Valley or Montage Healdsburg | Suites With Keith
four-seasons-napa-valley-vs-montage-heal.description: #02 and #03 on Keith's Napa & Sonoma ranking — Four Seasons standard in a Calistoga vineyard, or the Healdsburg hotel he's stayed at 20+ times.
four-seasons-napa-valley-vs-montage-heal.deck: #02 and #03 on my Napa & Sonoma ranking — one at genuine Four Seasons standard inside a working Calistoga vineyard, the other my most-returned-to hotel anywhere, twenty-plus stays in. They’re in different valleys, and they answer different trips.
four-seasons-napa-valley-vs-montage-heal.stamp: Four or five stays at one · 20+ at the other · #02 and #03 on my ranking

choose.h3: If the trip is a group
choose.lead: The rare wine-country hotel that fits families, couples, girls trips, and multi-couple groups equally well — gorgeous pools, a one-star Michelin restaurant in the vineyard, and service at genuine Four Seasons standard on every stay I’ve had.
choose.alt: Vineyard pools at Four Seasons Napa Valley, Calistoga

choose.h3: If it’s the two of you and the vines
choose.lead: Waking up and sitting by your own fire pit overlooking the vineyards never gets old — and after twenty-plus stays, it still hasn’t. Just outside downtown Healdsburg, with a complimentary shuttle to the plaza and the best restaurant view on my list.
choose.alt: Vineyard-room fire pit at Montage Healdsburg

rows: Napa — the Calistoga end: quieter, a longer drive to southern wineries
Sonoma — just outside downtown Healdsburg, shuttle to the plaza
Dark-moody or bright farmhouse; upper floor if outdoor-shower privacy matters
A vineyard room — the fire pit over the vines is the property’s magic
A one-star Michelin restaurant, plus the pool bar
The best restaurant view of any table on my list
Four Seasons service standard, consistent every stay
They remember you — one masseuse I book every single visit
four-seasons-napa-valley-vs-montage-heal.footnote: Both are Fora / Virtuoso preferred partners — and Four Seasons Napa runs third- or fourth-night-free offers through partner channels that meaningfully change the math on longer stays. Also know what you’re choosing geographically: Healdsburg is Sonoma, not Napa — more relaxed, less commercial, and my own preference.

verdict.h2: Groups go to Calistoga; couples go to Healdsburg.
paras: Four Seasons Napa Valley earned its spot the boring way: consistency. Since they worked out the early kinks, service has been at genuine Four Seasons standard on every stay, and it’s a property that genuinely lends itself to a large swath of people — which is rare at this level.

Montage is the one I keep going back to — at least twenty stays over the past few years, more than any other hotel on my list. Twenty stays in, I notice small things a first-timer wouldn’t, and the team always makes them right. Book the vineyard room; the mountain and oak categories are lovely but miss the signature view.

meadowood-vs-stanly-ranch.title: Meadowood or Stanly Ranch | Suites With Keith
meadowood-vs-stanly-ranch.description: Keith's #01 in wine country against the valley's boldest design statement — how to choose between the benchmark and the architecture.
meadowood-vs-stanly-ranch.deck: My #01 in wine country against the valley’s boldest design statement. One is the benchmark I measure every other Napa stay against; the other is the prettiest argument for choosing architecture over vineyards. Years of repeat stays inform both takes.
meadowood-vs-stanly-ranch.stamp: #01 and #06 on my Napa & Sonoma ranking · repeat stays at both

choose.h3: If you want to be taken care of
choose.lead: Service at Aman standards — the single biggest separator in wine country. Around 40 spacious, private cottages tucked into a wooded estate above St. Helena, and there really isn’t a bad room to be had.
choose.alt: Estate cottages at Meadowood, Napa Valley

choose.h3: If design and wellness are the trip
choose.lead: Possibly the most architecturally striking hotel in wine country, with arguably the prettiest spa in the valley, a large fire-pit terrace on every room, and Bear — one of the more interesting restaurants in Napa right now.
choose.alt: Modern ranch architecture at Stanly Ranch, Napa

rows: A private wooded estate above St. Helena
The Carneros marshes — not the vineyard postcard
Service, cottages, slow mornings around the spa
Architecture, the valley’s prettiest spa, Bear
~40 cottages — not a bad one among them
Every room has a large terrace with its own fire pit
Younger couples, wellness travelers, design lovers

meadowood-vs-stanly-ranch.footnote: Two practical notes: about 90% of Meadowood’s rooms aren’t fully accessible — buggies are available for mobility concerns — and booking it through a Virtuoso partner adds a credit, often $500, that meaningfully changes the math on a multi-night stay. At Stanly Ranch, terrace privacy varies by room — I’ll steer you to the best-sited ones.

verdict.h2: The benchmark, most of the time.
paras: There’s something about Meadowood that’s hard to put your finger on — Aman-quality service, a real sense of place, thoughtful turndown treats each evening. Every time I go, I feel well taken care of, and I can’t say that about every property on my list. That’s why it holds #01 after years of repeat stays across the valley.

Stanly Ranch is genuinely beautiful — but the location doesn’t quite deliver the classic wine-country feeling, and I don’t find myself wanting to go back as often as the hotels above it. If the vineyard postcard is the point of the trip, that’s Meadowood. If the spa and the architecture are the point, Stanly makes its case.

choose.alt: Wooded estate grounds at Meadowood

choose.lead: Set inside its own working vineyard in Calistoga, with a one-star Michelin restaurant, gorgeous pools, and the flexibility to host families, girls trips, and multi-couple groups as comfortably as couples.
choose.alt: Farmhouse rooms in the vineyard at Four Seasons Napa Valley

rows: Private wooded estate above St. Helena

paras: For a honeymoon, an anniversary, or any trip where the hotel is the celebration: Meadowood. Every time I go, I feel well taken care of — the service, the cottages, and the sense of place are why it’s the property I measure every other Napa stay against.

For everything else — the family trip, the girls trip, the four-couple harvest weekend — Four Seasons is the rare wine-country hotel that genuinely fits all of them, and the Michelin star and pool scene don’t hurt. Both are at the top of my list for a reason; the group decides this one, not the hotels.

kalesma-vs-cali-mykonos.title: Kalesma or Cali Mykonos | Suites With Keith
kalesma-vs-cali-mykonos.description: #07 and #08 on Keith's Greece top 10 — laid-back Cycladic design above Ornos, or independent polish on Mykonos's quiet east side.
kalesma-vs-cali-mykonos.deck: #07 and #08 on my Greece top 10, and the definitive Mykonos style question: laid-back Cycladic design above Ornos Bay, or independent polish on the quiet east side. Pick your flavor of Mykonos.

choose.lead: Cycladic minimalism in dark wood and marble that just works, set above Ornos Bay and central to everything — without any of the Mykonos Town chaos. The fire pit overlooking Delos at sunset is the memory that outlasts the trip.
choose.alt: Dark-wood Cycladic suites at Kalesma, above Ornos Bay

choose.h3: If space, privacy and the gym win
choose.lead: An independent stunner on the island’s quieter eastern side, with one of the largest infinity pools I saw in Greece, plunge pools that actually feel private — and the best hotel gym I have ever seen, anywhere.
choose.alt: The infinity pool at Cali Mykonos

kalesma-vs-cali-mykonos.footnote: Both are preferred partners — same rate as booking direct, with the extras layered on. Traveling with kids on Mykonos? Cali on the quieter east side is the pick I give families. And whichever you book, Pere Ubu at Kalesma is one of the island’s best sunset tables — reserve it the moment your trip is confirmed.

verdict.h2: Cali is flashier on paper — Kalesma won me over.
paras: Kalesma’s laid-back beauty is what stayed with me: a glass of wine in the jacuzzi at golden hour with the bay below, the fire pit at sunset before dinner, and a design language unlike anything else on the island. Dining is pleasant rather than the headline — and Mykonos’s remarkable restaurant scene is minutes away.

But Cali is a genuinely remarkable property I’d happily return to — refined, personal service, staff who greet you by name, and I’d stay again just for that gym. For fitness-minded travelers and privacy seekers, it settles the question by itself.

minos-beach-vs-minos-palace-crete.title: Minos Beach or Minos Palace | Suites With Keith

choose.h3: If the trip includes kids — or art
choose.lead: Arguably Crete’s first true luxury hotel, and it’s aged the way the best things do: 125 whitewashed bungalows in waterfront gardens, none more than about twenty steps from the sea, threaded with more than 55 site-specific artworks.
choose.alt: Waterfront bungalows at Minos Beach Art Hotel, Crete

choose.h3: If you want water on three sides
choose.lead: The adults-only sister on its own small peninsula — an island within an island, where all 148 rooms face the sea because there’s nowhere else to face, and a swim before breakfast is a ten-step commute.
choose.alt: The private peninsula at Minos Palace, Crete

And if what you actually want on this coast is a new-build with a private pool in every room, that’s Acro Suites — compared against the Palace in my adults-only Crete head-to-head.

verdict.h2: The family books the art hotel; the couple books the peninsula.
paras: Minos Beach is older in the best sense — established, shaded, unhurried, and unlike anywhere else on the island. Agios Nikolaos is under a mile away on foot, a genuine rarity for a resort of this kind, and worth using for the harbourfront tavernas.
Minos Palace occupies a piece of geography no new hotel will ever get again — and it’s the best value on my Crete shortlist. Quiet, surrounded by water, the definition of an easy recommendation.

Minos Palace is the other kind of answer: quiet, surrounded by water, and the best value on my Crete shortlist — the definition of an easy recommendation.

auberge-du-soleil-vs-montage-healdsburg.title: Auberge du Soleil or Montage Healdsburg | Suites With Keith
auberge-du-soleil-vs-montage-healdsburg.description: Only two American wine-country hotels made The Fifteen, Keith's honeymoon shortlist — the Rutherford terrace or the vineyard bungalows. Here's how he splits them.
auberge-du-soleil-vs-montage-healdsburg.deck: Only two American wine-country properties made The Fifteen — my shortlist of honeymoon hotels I’d book anywhere in the world. Auberge du Soleil carries the Napa flag at #14; Montage Healdsburg carries Sonoma’s at #15. This is how I split them.
auberge-du-soleil-vs-montage-healdsburg.stamp: #14 and #15 on The Fifteen · the shortlist’s only wine-country entries · both Fora / Virtuoso partners

choose.h3: If the terrace is the honeymoon
choose.lead: The original Napa luxury property, perched on the Rutherford hillside — still the most romantic seat in the valley. My note beside it on The Fifteen names the three reasons: the terrace, the valley, the wine list.

choose.h3: If you want to live among the vines
choose.lead: Vineyard bungalows and a slower pace — waking up by your own fire pit overlooking the vines never gets old, and after twenty-plus stays it still hasn’t. The best restaurant view of any table on my list.

rows: #15 — the Sonoma entry (and #03 on my Napa & Sonoma ranking)
Elevated above the valley floor — the whole stay looks over the vines
Your own fire-pit terrace over the vineyards
The most famous dining terrace in the valley — the view that made it a legend
The best restaurant view on my list
One of the three reasons it made my shortlist — in the region where that bar is highest
Healdsburg’s wineries minutes away, shuttle to the plaza
Adults-first — the romance is the product
auberge-du-soleil-vs-montage-healdsburg.footnote: At Auberge, book the terrace with the room — the famous tables go as fast as the rooms do, so I reserve both together. Families are better matched elsewhere on my Napa & Sonoma list. Both are Fora / Virtuoso preferred partners: same rate as direct, credits and extras layered on.

verdict.h2: Two seats on The Fifteen — one of them is yours.
paras: Auberge du Soleil can be summarized in six words and lose nothing: the terrace, the valley, the wine list. For the couple who wants the classic Napa romance — dinner above the valley as the light goes — it’s still the most romantic seat in wine country.

Montage trades that elevation for intimacy with the vines themselves — the bungalow, the fire pit, the slower Healdsburg pace. It’s the hotel I’ve returned to more than any other, anywhere. Tell me your couple and I’ll tell you which.

santorini-vs-mykonos.title: Santorini or Mykonos | Suites With Keith
santorini-vs-mykonos.description: The Cyclades' two headliners, compared by an advisor who toured 38 hotels across the islands — which one your trip actually wants, and the hotel calls inside each.
santorini-vs-mykonos.deck: The two islands with real international airports, and the two carrying the biggest reputations in Greece. I worked both on my Cyclades trip — here’s which one your trip actually wants, and the hotel decisions waiting inside whichever you pick.
santorini-vs-mykonos.stamp: From my 38-hotel Cyclades trip · the two islands you can fly into from outside Greece

choose.h3: If the caldera is the reason you’re coming
choose.lead: The island that introduced the world to Cycladic luxury. It earns its reputation for two or three nights in a caldera suite — the cave rooms, the plunge pools, the sunset — and it’s the crescendo of any route: finish here, don’t start.
choose.alt: The caldera at Santorini

choose.h3: If you want range — the loud island and the quiet one
choose.lead: I expected a party island and found some of the best hotels, meals and service of my entire trip through the Cyclades. It’s genuinely two islands — and which one you get depends almost entirely on what was booked before you landed.
choose.alt: A protected bay on Mykonos

rows: Two or three in a caldera suite — then move on
Three days is the right length for most people
The crowds — by seven the Oia castle is shoulder to shoulder
It punishes the unplanned — tables and beach beds go weeks out
Cave suites on the cliff — Canaves Oia, Andronis Boutique, Epitome
Real range: Kalesma’s design, Bill & Coo’s bay, Fouquet’s scene, Cali’s quiet
Couples and groups both — beach clubs by day, serious tables at night
The caldera cruise, the wineries, the rim walk
A private boat to Delos, Rhenia or Tinos — the best day happens off the island
The finale — ending here frees the best hotels
The entry point — fly in, move south through the Cyclades
santorini-vs-mykonos.footnote: You don’t actually have to choose: Mykonos 2 → Paros 3 → Santorini 3 is the full-arc route on my island pairings page, and the crossings between neighbours run under two hours. What I’d push back on is starting on Santorini — it’s the bar the rest of the trip gets measured against, and arriving day one ties you to whichever caldera hotel has space that night.

verdict.h2: First time, planning around dinner and the view: Santorini — as the finale.
paras: Santorini earns its reputation, and for a first trip built around the classic picture it’s the answer — two or three nights in a caldera suite, booked well ahead, placed at the end of the route so it’s the last thing you see rather than the measuring stick.

But Mykonos was the island that surprised me most — substance where I expected only scene. If your trip is as much about the beach day, the boat day and the table as the view, it’s the stronger base — provided the bookings are made before you land. And the honest answer for most ten-night trips is both, with Paros in between.

paros-vs-mykonos.title: Paros or Mykonos | Suites With Keith
paros-vs-mykonos.description: Keith's honest split between the Cyclades' two lookers — 45 minutes apart by ferry, and very different trips.
paros-vs-mykonos.deck: Paros has Mykonos’s good looks, better food, and about a third of the attitude — it’s where I send most people first. But Mykonos is the one with the international airport, the beach clubs, and some of the best hotels and meals of my entire Cyclades trip. Forty-five minutes of ferry separate two very different weeks.
paros-vs-mykonos.stamp: Where I send most people first · vs the island that punishes the unplanned

choose.h3: If you plan around dinner
choose.lead: Mykonos’s good looks, better food, a third of the attitude. Naousa’s restaurants on foot, sailing days to Despotiko’s empty beaches, and Parīlio — my most-booked hotel on the island, where families are genuinely welcome.
choose.alt: Naousa, Paros

choose.h3: If the scene is part of the trip
choose.lead: Beach clubs as the native art form, tables worth planning a trip around, and hotels from Kalesma’s composed design to Fouquet’s south-coast energy. Genuinely two islands — the loud one and the quiet one — if the bookings are made early.
choose.alt: A Mykonos beach day

rows: The point, for the right traveler
Better — and Naousa’s restaurants are on foot
Serious tables, reserved weeks out: ZUMA, Kiki’s, Scorpios at sunset
Small airport served mainly from Athens, or ferry
Parīlio (my most-booked on Paros) and Cosme on the Naousa beachfront
Kalesma, Bill & Coo Coast, Fouquet’s, Cali — four I’ve toured in person
Parīlio has a proper kids’ program
Cali on the quiet east side is the family pick; Bill & Coo is 17+
A sailing day from Paros to Despotiko — the day my clients talk about most
A private boat to Delos and Rhenia, or across to Tinos
paros-vs-mykonos.footnote: The crossing is 45 to 60 minutes, which is why my full-arc route does both: Mykonos 2 → Paros 3 → Santorini 3. Fly into Mykonos, take the energy first, then let Paros slow the trip down. September rates are approximate entry-level starting points from my matrix — ask me for your dates.

verdict.h2: Where I send most people first: Paros.
paras: For most couples — and every family — Paros is the better week: the food, the walkable evenings, the sailing day, and design hotels that cost meaningfully less than their Mykonos equivalents.

But if the version of the trip you’re picturing has a beach club in it, book Mykonos and book it properly — the island rewards planning more than any other in Greece, and with the tables and beds held early, it delivers substance the reputation doesn’t advertise. Or take the ferry and do both.

paros-vs-milos.title: Paros or Milos | Suites With Keith
paros-vs-milos.description: The eating island or the swimming island — Keith's split between the two Cyclades he pairs with Santorini most often.
paros-vs-milos.eyebrow: Head-to-head · The eating one or the swimming one
paros-vs-milos.deck: These are the two islands I pair with Santorini most often, and they answer different trips: Paros if you plan around dinner, Milos if you want to be in the water every day. Both keep small Athens-served airports — and both are the reason the middle of a route beats its bookends.
paros-vs-milos.stamp: The eating one vs the swimming one · both from my Cyclades trip

choose.h3: If the table sets the day
choose.lead: Mykonos’s good looks, better food, a third of the attitude. Naousa on foot at night, a sailing day to Despotiko’s empty beaches, and hotels — Parīlio, Cosme — that photograph well and still work when you’re actually living in them.
choose.alt: Naousa harbor, Paros

choose.h3: If the water sets the day
choose.lead: Volcanic rock and impossible water — Milos looks like nowhere else in Greece, and it’s best seen from a boat. Kleftiko’s sculpted white cliffs are the reason you came; Sarakiniko’s moonscape is the encore.
choose.alt: Volcanic coastline on Milos

A boat day — Kleftiko is the island; the roads are the supporting act
Classic Cycladic — Naousa’s harbor and whitewash

Parīlio (families welcome, my most-booked) and beachfront Cosme

Skinopi is bring-almost-nothing simple; Erēma is the resort option
Small airport from Athens, or ferry
Small airport from Athens, or ferry
Roughly two hours by high-speed boat
Roughly two hours by high-speed boat
paros-vs-milos.footnote: Both pair beautifully with Santorini — they’re routes B and C on my pairings page: Milos 4 → Santorini 3 for the swimming trip, Paros 4 → Santorini 3 for the eating one. September rates are approximate entry-level starting points; ask me for your dates.

verdict.h2: Plan around dinner: Paros. Be in the water every day: Milos.
paras: That’s genuinely the whole decision, and it’s why these two are my B and C pairings with Santorini rather than rivals — they solve different trips.

If you can’t choose, the tell is the boat: on Milos the boat day isn’t an excursion, it’s the island — you experience Milos from the water or you miss it. If that sentence excites you, book Milos. If you’d rather be walking to dinner in Naousa while someone else worries about the wind, that’s Paros.

milos-vs-sifnos.title: Milos or Sifnos | Suites With Keith
milos-vs-sifnos.description: The middle of Keith's island matrix, where he spends most of his own time — the swimming island or the food island.
milos-vs-sifnos.eyebrow: Head-to-head · The middle of the matrix
milos-vs-sifnos.deck: This is the part of the matrix where I spend most of my own time — real islands with real hotels, enough infrastructure to be comfortable and not enough to be crowded. If you only trust one recommendation from my island writing, make it this pair. The choice between them is the day versus the evening.
milos-vs-sifnos.stamp: Where I spend my own time · neighbours — most crossings here run under two hours

choose.h3: If you came for the water
choose.lead: Volcanic rock and impossible water — it looks like nowhere else in Greece and it’s best seen from a boat. Kleftiko, Sarakiniko, and swim stops you can’t reach by road.
choose.alt: Kleftiko's white cliffs, Milos

choose.h3: If you came for the table
choose.lead: The food island — and it earns the title. This is where Greek cooking gets taken seriously by people who live there, not by people importing a concept. Eat your way through Apollonia and Kastro; linger.
choose.alt: Kastro village, Sifnos

rows: The food one — some islands ask you to see more; Sifnos asks you to linger

A food walk through Apollonia and Kastro
Skinopi Lodge (no pool, no restaurant — on purpose) or Erēma, new in 2026

Outdoor kitchens and a breakfast basket on your Skinopi terrace
Bostani at Verina Astra — cooked from the hotel’s own garden, sold out early every year
Small airport served from Athens, or ferry
No airport at all — a ferry leg mid-trip, which is most of why it’s still quiet
milos-vs-sifnos.footnote: Booking note from the matrix: Verina Astra’s dinner and rooms sell out early every single year — if Sifnos is next summer’s trip, book it now, genuinely. And Erēma on Milos is the same group behind Parīlio and Cosme — Paros then Milos is a trip I’d happily build.

verdict.h2: In the water every day: Milos. At the table every night: Sifnos.
paras: These two are the heart of the matrix’s middle — the islands I’d pick for second-timers and the quiet-seeking, and the ones I keep going back to myself.

And they’re neighbours in a part of the Cyclades where crossings run short — so the honest answer for a week is the E-route philosophy: take the quiet middle seriously, do both, and let Santorini be the finale rather than the trip.

napa-vs-sonoma.title: Napa or Sonoma | Suites With Keith
napa-vs-sonoma.description: After staying at nearly every luxury hotel in both valleys, here's how Keith splits wine country — the polish or the pace.
napa-vs-sonoma.deck: I’ve personally stayed at nearly every luxury hotel in both valleys. My #01 and #02 are both Napa — and yet the hotel I’ve returned to more than any other, anywhere, is in Sonoma. That contradiction is the whole decision, so here it is honestly.
napa-vs-sonoma.stamp: Nearly every luxury hotel in both valleys, stayed · my ranking on file

choose.h3: If the trip is the classic
choose.lead: The benchmark end of wine country: Meadowood’s Aman-standard service above St. Helena, Four Seasons inside its own working Calistoga vineyard with a Michelin star on property, Auberge’s famous terrace over the valley.
choose.alt: The wooded estate at Meadowood, Napa Valley

choose.h3: If you want it relaxed
choose.lead: Healdsburg is a more relaxed, less commercial base — and my own preference. Montage’s vineyard rooms with their fire pits are the reason I’ve stayed twenty-plus times, with a complimentary shuttle to the plaza so nobody argues about who’s driving home from dinner.
choose.alt: Vineyard rooms at Montage Healdsburg, Sonoma

napa-vs-sonoma.footnote: Every hotel named here is a Fora / Virtuoso preferred partner — same rate as booking direct, with the credits and extras layered on, and on multi-night stays those offers genuinely change the math. The full nine-hotel ranking, from personal stays, is on my Napa & Sonoma page.

verdict.h2: My ranking says Napa. My calendar says Sonoma.
paras: For the celebration — the honeymoon, the milestone anniversary, the trip where the hotel is the event — Napa wins on the strength of Meadowood and Four Seasons alone. Every time I go to Meadowood I feel well taken care of, and I can’t say that about every property on my list.

But the trip I actually keep taking is Healdsburg: twenty-plus stays at Montage and counting. If wine country is going to become your place rather than your occasion, that’s the valley — more relaxed, less commercial, and the fire pit over the vines never gets old. Tell me which trip this is, and I’ll tell you which valley.
